chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil narrated from Abu Shibl, who said:

I was present with Yunus al-Shaybani while Abu Abdullah عليه السلام was informing him about the blood monies. So I said to him: If the nutfah came out mixed and stirred with blood? He said: “It has become an ʿalaqah. If it is pure blood, then in it is forty. And if it is black blood, then nothing is due upon him except taʿzir, because whatever is of pure blood, that is for the child, and whatever is of black blood, that is only from the inside of the body.”

Abu Shibl said: What if the ʿalaqah has come to have in it something like a vein of flesh? He said: “In it are forty-two and a tenth.” I said: One-tenth of forty is four. He said: “It is only one-tenth of the muḍghah, because only one-tenth of it has gone. And whenever it increases, it is increased until it reaches sixty.”

He said: I said: I saw in the muḍghah something like a knotted form, a dry bone. He said: “That is the bone, for which at the first stage there are four dinars. If it increases, then add four, until it completes eighty. And likewise when the bone is clothed with flesh, then likewise.”

He said: I said: If he struck her and the child fell, and it is not known whether it had been alive or not? He said: “Far from it, O Abu Shibl. When five months have passed, life has come to be in it, and it has incurred the blood money.”

key_terms.الدِّيَاتِ: blood monies or financial compensations for injury or killing
key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: the legally mandated blood money compensation
key_terms.النُّطْفَةَ: the sperm-drop or earliest embryonic stage
key_terms.الْخَمْسَةُ الْأَشْهُرِ: the five-month stage after which life is recognized in the fetus
key_terms.الْعَلَقَةَ: the clinging clot stage of embryonic development
key_terms.الْمُضْغَةِ: the chewed-like lump stage of embryonic development

ai.seo_question: What are the diyyah rulings for miscarriage and fetal injury at different stages of development in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings on diyyah for miscarriage and fetal injury at different stages of development, from nutfah to ʿalaqah, muḍghah, bone, and the more developed fetus. It distinguishes between blood related to the fetus and blood from the mother's body, and it states that after five months the fetus is regarded as having life such that diyyah becomes obligatory.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5318 - It was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil from Abu Shibl who said:

I was present with Yunus Al-Shaybani while Abu Abdullah (as) was informing him about blood money (diyat).
I asked Imam (as): "What if the sperm-drop (nutfah) came out mixed with blood?"
Imam (as) replied: "If it has clotted and the blood is pure, then it is forty dinars. But if it is black blood, then there is nothing upon him except disciplinary punishment (taʿzir), because pure blood is for the child, while black blood is from within the body."

Abu Shibl asked: "What if the clot (Alaqah) has a vein-like piece of flesh in it?"
Imam (as) replied: "It is forty-two dinars, with one-tenth of it."
I asked: "Is one-tenth of forty not four?"
Imam (as) said: "It is one-tenth of the muḍghah (chewed-like substance) because only one-tenth of it was lost. As it grows, the amount increases until it reaches sixty."

I asked: "I saw in the muḍghah something like a solid bone knot."
Imam (as) said: "That is the bone, which initially starts with four dinars. If it increases, then add four more until it completes eighty dinars. Similarly, when the bone is covered with flesh, it follows the same ruling."

I asked: "If a woman was struck, causing the fetus to miscarry and it is not known whether the fetus was alive or not?"
Imam (as) replied: "Far from it, O' Abu Shibl! Once five months have passed, life has been instilled in it, and full blood money (diyyah) becomes obligatory."
